title: India Women's Cricket Team Secures Olympic Berth for LA 2028 Games
excerpt: The ICC confirmed India among the first four women's teams to qualify for cricket's return to the Olympics after 128 years, based on their performance at the T20 World Cup 2026 in England.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India's women's cricket team qualified for the LA 2028 Olympics as Asia's top team.
  • Cricket returns to the Olympics after 128 years, with six teams competing in T20 events.
  • Australia, Great Britain, and South Africa also secured Olympic berths alongside India.
  • The men's qualification depends on ICC T20I rankings by December 31, 2026.
Cricket's Olympic Comeback
›Cricket last featured in the Olympics in 1900.
›LA 2028 will host six teams in men's and women's T20 events.
›28 matches will be played across both events.
›Qualification includes representation from Africa, Asia, Europe, and Oceania.
  • India qualified for the LA 2028 Olympics women's cricket competition as Asia's highest-placed team at the Women's T20 World Cup 2026 in England.
  • Australia, Great Britain (via England) and South Africa also secured berths, with cricket returning to the Olympics after 128 years.
  • Six teams will compete in each of the men's and women's T20 events at a purpose-built venue in Pomona, California.
  • The men's qualification pathway relies on ICC T20I rankings as of December 31, 2026, with India needing to finish as Asia's top-ranked side.

India's women's cricket team has secured a place at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, becoming one of the first four nations confirmed for cricket's historic return to the world's biggest sporting event. The International Cricket Council (ICC) and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) jointly announced the qualification pathway on June 29, confirming India's berth alongside Australia, Great Britain (via England) and South Africa.

The qualification came through the ongoing Women's T20 World Cup 2026 in England, where India emerged as the highest-placed eligible team from Asia. Each continent was capped at one qualifying spot. The announcement arrived a day after India's group-stage exit from the tournament, a bittersweet coda to a campaign that began with promise but ended with defeats to South Africa and Australia.

Cricket Returns After 128 Years

Cricket was last played at the Olympic Games at the 1900 Paris Games, making its return to LA 2028 a milestone 128 years in the making. Six nations will compete in each of the men's and women's T20 competitions at a purpose-built cricket venue in Pomona, California, with a combined 28 matches across both events.

The qualification structure guarantees representation from Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania. Five spots are determined through ICC events and T20I rankings, while the sixth will be decided at the inaugural ICC Olympics Qualifier in 2027, featuring eight nations.

ICC Chief Executive Sanjog Gupta called the inclusion a "unique showcase on global sport's grandest stage," adding that the sport's return would provide "the Olympic movement a gateway into the hearts and minds of more than two billion cricket fans."

India's World Cup Campaign and Olympic Silver Lining

Harmanpreet Kaur's squad entered the Women's T20 World Cup 2026 as one of the pre-tournament favourites, riding the momentum of their ODI World Cup triumph at home in 2025. India opened with wins over Pakistan and the Netherlands before a loss to South Africa disrupted their campaign. A victory against Bangladesh kept hopes alive, but a defeat to Australia in the final group match ended their run.

Despite the group-stage exit, India's overall standing as Asia's top-performing side was enough to clinch the continental quota place for the Olympics. The ICC's qualification framework, which was not announced before the tournament began, retroactively used the World Cup results to allocate continental berths.

India's Path to the Olympics
›India qualified as Asia's highest-placed team at the T20 World Cup 2026.
›India's campaign included wins over Pakistan and the Netherlands.
›Group-stage exit followed losses to South Africa and Australia.
›Qualification framework retroactively used World Cup results.

The West Indies Problem and Host Qualification

The qualification pathway exposed a structural wrinkle: the West Indies, one of the tournament's semi-finalists, are ineligible for the Olympics because they are a composite of Caribbean nations and not recognised as an IOC National Olympic Committee. However, if their teams rank among the top eight non-qualified sides by December 31, 2026, a dedicated Caribbean Qualifier will determine which individual nation represents the region at the ICC Olympics Qualifier.

The United States, as hosts, can qualify automatically for both men's and women's events provided they appear in the top 15 of the ICC T20I rankings at any point between June 30 and December 31, 2026. The US men's team, currently ranked 13th, is well-positioned. The women's team, ranked 20th, has been excluded as neither they nor any team from the Americas features in the ICC's top 15, according to Reuters.

What the Olympics Mean for Indian Cricket Fans Abroad

For Indians in the United States and across the global diaspora, cricket at the LA Olympics represents an unprecedented convergence of two worlds. The sport's inclusion at a Games hosted in a major Indian diaspora hub — Los Angeles County is home to one of the largest Indian-American communities in the US — brings the possibility of watching India compete in cricket on American soil at the highest level.

The purpose-built venue in Pomona, roughly 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, will host all matches. Qualified nations will select 15-player squads, with teams divided into groups of three. Each team plays the others in its group once, then plays two cross-group matches. The top two sides contest for gold and silver, while third and fourth compete for bronze.

What's Next

For the men's competition, four direct Olympic berths will be awarded based on ICC T20I rankings as of December 31, 2026. India, as reigning men's T20 World Cup champions, must finish as Asia's highest-ranked eligible side to secure a direct ticket to Los Angeles. The fifth spot goes to the USA if they meet ranking criteria, while the sixth will be determined through the 2027 qualifier.

The ICC Olympics Qualifier 2027 — dates and host nation still to be confirmed — will feature eight nations in each of the men's and women's draws, offering the final pathway to LA 2028.
